title: Bench-align a prosthetic foot: 30 mm ahead of the laser line, toes out 5 degrees
instruction: Bench-align the right prosthetic foot on the grey jig plate. First put the orange heel block flat on the plate where the heel will rest. Then set the foot on the plate, sole down, with its heel on the block and its toe on the plate: the middle of the foot's length 30 mm in front of the red laser line, the heel on the dark centre line, and the toe end turned out about 5 degrees toward your right. Then let go and move both grippers clear of the foot and the block.
context: Prosthetists (O*NET 29-2091.00) and prosthetic technicians (51-9082.00, Medical Appliance Technicians) bench-align every new below-knee prosthesis in an alignment jig before the first fitting. The foot makers' bench-alignment instructions set the foot first: its heel raised on a block to the shoe's effective heel height (heel height minus forefoot sole thickness) plus 5 mm, the middle of its length about 30 mm in front of the reference line the jig's laser projects, and its toes turned out about 5 degrees. The socket is then built up over the laser line. A foot set too far back throws the knee into flexion and drops the patient off the toe; too far forward, roll-over feels like walking uphill and the knee is pushed back; a wrong toe-out loads the knee sideways. Errors found only at the fitting cost clinic time while the patient waits. Here the shoe's effective heel height is 15 mm, so the block is 20 mm.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Three things are on the table. (1) Jig plate: a fixed light-grey anodised aluminium plate, 300 x 200 x 6 mm, covering x 15 to 45 cm, y -10 to +10 cm, with two 4 mm wide lines inlaid flush in its top (paint or tape on the real plate; no ridges): a bright red laser line across it (along y), centred at x 27.0 cm, standing for the reference line the jig's laser projects, and a dark grey centre line along it (along x), centred at y 0, the line of progression. In simulation it is seven fixed boxes with flush tops: four grey quarters, the red line and the two halves of the dark line. (2) Heel block: a loose rigid orange polyurethane block, 60 x 70 x 20 mm (60 mm along x), 50 g, lying flat on the table centred at x 25.0 cm, y +40.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y; its 20 mm is the shoe's 15 mm effective heel height plus 5 mm. (3) Right prosthetic foot: a loose rigid stand-in of a right foot, 250 g, a 3D-printed beige plastic shell with a flat 220 x 70 mm sole, made of three boxes: a rear shell (heel and midfoot) 120 x 70 x 28 mm, a forefoot shell 100 x 70 x 16 mm in front of it with the two soles flush, and a black 3D-printed plastic block, 46 x 46 x 30 mm, standing for the pyramid adapter on the rear shell's top, its centre 85 mm from the heel end (its top 58 mm above the sole). Mass is spread evenly: the centre of mass is 94 mm from the heel end and 17 mm above the sole. The foot lies sole down on the table, toes along +x: heel end at x 19.0 cm, toe end at x 41.0 cm, long axis on y -38.0 cm (the adapter's centre at x 27.5 cm). Its heel point H is the middle of the heel end's bottom edge, its toe point T the middle of the toe end's bottom edge, and its middle M is halfway between them. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored at the end of the trial from the objects' poses (never their bounding boxes). Heel to toe is the direction from H to T seen from above. Gate, else 0: all four sole corners are over the plate seen from above; the foot is sole down (its up axis within 15 degrees of vertical); heel to toe is within 20 degrees of +x; H is within 15 mm of the centre line sideways; each arm's tool point and pad-tip point is 20 mm or more from every box of the foot and from the block (let go and moved clear, as the instruction asks; arms that cannot be read count as not let go); and H, T and the block's centre each moved less than 2 mm (path length) over the last 0.5 s. A foot that passes the gate scores 0.25, plus 0.25 for each check met: (A) forward: M is 25 to 35 mm in front of the laser line's centre (x 27.0 cm); (B) toe-out: heel to toe is turned 2 to 8 degrees from +x toward -y, the robot's right (with a ruler: the y of H minus the y of T is 3.5 to 14.1 % of the x of T minus the x of H, 7.6 to 30.6 mm over the pitched foot's 218 mm); (C) heel on the block: the block lies flat on the plate (its 20 mm axis within 10 degrees of vertical, either face down, its lowest point within 3 mm of the plate's top), its centre is within 35 mm of the line through H and T sideways and no more than 30 mm behind H along that line, none of its corners (seen from above) is more than 90 mm in front of H along that line (4 mm behind the foot's centre of mass, 94 mm from H, so the foot stays heel on block, toe on plate by itself; for a block square to the foot: its centre at most 60 mm in front of H), H is 18 to 40 mm above the plate's top and T is within 4 mm of it. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0; every end state gets exactly one of them. Examples: foot aligned with no block under it: 0.75; toed in (toe toward +y) or square: no (B); block under the toe or the midfoot: no (C); foot still held or a gripper left within 20 mm of it, on its side, backwards or partly off the plate: 0; nothing done: 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise the end state at the run limit is scored. In a real trial: mark H, T and M on the foot's sides and square them down to the plate, measure M from the laser line, H and T from the centre line and the block's front corners from H along the foot with a ruler, the heel's height above the plate with a ruler, and take a photo from above.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with default friction. The foot is a stand-in: a flat-soled shell of two boxes with a thinner forefoot and a box for the pyramid adapter, of uniform density; it rests on the block's front edge and its toe end, not on a rounded heel and a rocker sole. The laser's reference plane is a red line on a plate of flush boxes (a part slid over a seam may catch). The jig's socket side is out of scope. The scorer reads each gripper's tool and pad-tip points, not its fingers.
reset_notes: Lay the heel block flat on the table centred at x 25.0 cm, y +40.0 cm, sides parallel to x and y; lay the foot sole down, toes along +x, its long axis on y -38.0 cm with the heel end at x 19.0 cm. The plate is fixed. Nothing is consumed.
